shell-injected-env: The sidecar process this TS ran in carried GAMELIB_SHELL_EXE, GAMELIB_APP_ROOT, GAMELIB_STEAM_ROOT_DEFAULT and GAMELIB_STORE_BOOT, injected by src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs. A spawn from the shell own environment does not carry them, so the Rust runner env is the golden env without those four keys. No golden here holds them (the cases run on the pinned base env), so the Rust side adds none and the delta only records the rule for the cases that compare against a sidecar-run recording.
random-abort-id: A call with no abortId and no app name takes Math.random().toString() as its abort id and track key. The cases pin Math.random to a fixed value, so the golden holds that string; the Rust runner takes a unique id of its own and the comparison replaces it.
chunk-boundaries: Where one stdout or stderr chunk ends is an operating-system artefact: Node and the Rust reader both take what a pipe read returns, up to 64 KiB, and a child that writes in bursts is cut at different places on different systems. The scripted replay hands the Rust runner the recorded chunks as they were, so a chunk boundary is never compared against a real pipe; runner_real.rs covers the real reads. The result window keeps the last 50 chunks, so a run that crosses the window with different cuts can keep different text; that quirk (the window counts chunks, not bytes) is filed as a todo and kept as recorded.
spawn-error-text: The message of a spawn failure is the one the operating system gives the spawning side: Node reports `spawn <bin> ENOENT`, the Rust runner reports `spawn <bin>: <OS error text>`. The replay of a case whose recorded error starts with `spawn ` compares that the Rust error starts with `spawn `, that stderr equals the error, and every other field of the result and the Error running command line prefix; the text after it is not compared.
windows-path-separator: The win32 cases were recorded on a POSIX host, where Node path.join joins with a slash; on Windows it joins with a backslash, and the Rust runner joins with the separator of the platform it is told it runs on. The replay on any host substitutes, in the actual output, the backslash-joined runner path with the slash-joined one before comparing, so only the separator of that one joined path is excused and every other character (the doubled backslashes inside PowerShell arguments included) is compared as recorded.
test-local-sanitizer: The TS callRunner takes any function as logSanitizer; the Rust runner takes only the two named sanitizers (gogAuth, nileAuth). One recorded case hands it a sanitizer local to the test, 'mask-secret' (line.replace('SECRET', '***')), which neither named sanitizer reproduces and which is not part of the product. The replay runs that case with no sanitizer and compares everything except the text of the raw entries written to the log writers: those are the recorded masked text on the golden side and the unmasked chunk on the Rust side, blanked on both sides, and the golden side is checked to hold no SECRET. The result, the stream the observer sees (raw in both), the window, the order and count of writes per writer and every other log entry are compared as recorded. The arbitrary-function hook itself is not ported (filed as a todo); the order (writers sanitized, observer and window raw) is proved by a unit test in call_runner.rs and the sanitizers' own answers by golden_redaction.
game-merged-streams: A game-class run (the runner.call.launch cases) writes both of its output streams to one capture file that Rust tails, so Rust cannot tell stdout from stderr and reads in chunks of its own. The replay compares a game case with: the chunks the observer saw and the raw entries written to one log writer joined into the one text they make; a result that ended on its own answering the whole printed text (trimmed) as stdout with no stderr; and the text the error handler was given with whitespace left out (the helper's per-chunk trim takes whitespace the merged text keeps). The order and count of every other entry, the spawn (program, argv, env, cwd, class), the abort and error calls, the general log lines and every failure, signal, abort and cancellation result are compared as recorded.
